title: Queue a touches-sweep citation stub only when the cited decision has left the active set
action: Gate the log-time touches-sweep on active-set membership (D1). The sweep is the `if let Some(ids) = &touches` block at verbs_read.rs:818-843, which today calls sweep_decision_citations and add_capture_stub for EVERY touched id. Hoist the existing `let active = active_decisions(root, false)?;` read from :845 to just above that block and reuse it — do not add a second read. Both the sweep and that read already sit after the append_jsonl at :802, so hoisting keeps the property its comment at :805-806 names: it reads the same active-set shape every other active_decisions() caller sees. Then, for each touched_id, skip the whole per-id sweep when that id IS present in the active set — a touches: relation whose target is still active queues nothing at all. When the id is absent, behave exactly as today: walk sweep_decision_citations, apply touches_sweep_excluded unchanged (D3), and enqueue a stub per surviving hit. Do NOT touch do_supersede's own sweep (D2), the impact door, the close-time sweep, or any already-queued stub (D4). Author inline tests in this file's test module covering: a touches: on a live decision queues NOTHING; a touches: on a retired decision still queues one stub per citing doc; the existing file exclusions still apply on that retired path; and a decision carrying both relations keeps its retiring-path behaviour.
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee --bin bee decisions

truths: Logging a decision whose touches: target is still active queues no capture stub
Logging a decision whose touches: target has been retired still queues one stub per citing document
The sweep on the retiring relation behaves exactly as before

prohibitions: No change to the impact door or to stubs already queued
